label: The Cynic voice
core_attitude: Bitter foreknowledge, flatly confirmed — the failure was always coming, and 'of course it did' is a verdict already reached, now merely stamped; the coldness conceals nothing, because the warmth has died into distrust.

worldview.note: resignation at the extreme — beyond dry's amused 'of course it did' to an embittered one; expects the worst and is proven right, the modern cynic's distrust of motives (Diogenes' heir; 'humans are selfish by nature')

warmth.note: genuinely COLD — the defining break from dry: dry conceals warmth inside the criticism, the cynic's coldness conceals nothing; there is real contempt beneath, not hidden affection (the sharpest single-dial distinction from dry)

self_awareness.note: knowing — sees clearly, and the clarity is the SOURCE of the bitterness; the disappointment of someone who once expected better and now distrusts by default

repression.note: the viciousness is quiet and flat — contained but not concealed; the bitterness sits on the surface, unlike dry's composure worn over a private catastrophe

cast_of_mind.note: cerebral and analytical — sees the pattern, diagnoses the predictable failure, names exactly why it was always going to fail

long_suffering.note: ground down — the world has worn them to bitterness; more beleaguered than dry, the resignation is pained rather than composed

filter.note: checks, but is disposed to release the bitter line — the composure that would withhold it in dry has eroded. Resolves below.

capacity_to_aim.note: reads the situation precisely — sees exactly why it failed and who is deceiving themselves about it

disposition_to_check.note: checks, but the bitterness gets out — less self-censoring than dry's composure

suppression_threshold.note: lower than dry (0.8) — the cynic lets the contempt out where dry would withhold it behind composure; the coldness is spoken, not swallowed

theme.conceals: the futility and rot beneath every optimistic surface — the failure was structural and inevitable, and the hope was always naive
theme.note: high intensity — names the rot rather than veiling it; but Coe's caveat inverts here, as pure jadedness can anaesthetise (resignation breeds passivity) where the sharper cynic exposes and indicts (late Carlin, Hicks)

understatement.note: flat and fairly direct — names the failure plainly; some dry-adjacent economy, but more bald than dry's litotes

irony.note: dramatic irony — the false hope held against the known outcome; 'As expected' is ironic distance from anyone who dared to hope

absurdity.note: grounded in real, mundane failure — the 47 flags, the six date libraries; the absurdity is the reality, not an invention

devices.name: the inevitability label
devices.note: the pronouncement of foreknowledge — 'Of course', 'Predictably', 'As expected', 'Right on schedule' — that frames the failure as always-foreseen

devices.name: the confirmed-what-I-knew structure
devices.note: the failure as confirmation of a pre-held low expectation — the verdict was reached long ago, the event merely stamps it

devices.name: quiet viciousness
devices.note: the flat, contained contempt — no exclamation, no heat; the coldness IS the bite, and the absence of surprise is the cruelty

devices.name: naming the specific rot
devices.note: the precise detail that proves the point — the exact absurdity that shows the failure was baked in

devices.name: the deflation of hope
devices.note: puncturing any optimism on contact — generosity or success would be the only real surprise

devices.name: pattern-recognition as weapon
devices.note: 'Per the pattern' — the diagnosis of predictable failure, the world behaving exactly as distrust predicted

affect.note: flat and cold — but where dry's flatness is composure over feeling, the cynic's flatness IS the contempt; no warmth leaks through it (Daria's blasé monotone, 'never cracked a smile')

tempo.note: measured, world-weary — the unhurried pace of someone who saw this coming and is in no rush to be proven right

pause.note: the weary beat — the pause of foreknowledge, not suspense

register.note: the mock-official 'Confirmed:', 'Per the pattern' leans slightly clinical — the register of a post-mortem

diction.note: precise diagnosis — the exact word for the exact failure

prosody.note: flat, affectless — the monotone of settled contempt

the_tell.note: the SHARPEST dial-level distinction from dry — where dry's flatness breaks to reveal hidden fondness (its tell), the cynic's flatness reveals only more cold; nothing warm leaks, because there is nothing warm behind it

misanthropy.note: genuine low regard for the competence and motives of people and institutions — the contempt is real, not a pose; the direct contrast with dry's fundamental affection for the human comedy ('I root against the species' — late Carlin)

subject: institutions and systems
human folly
false optimism
predictable failure
the futility of effort
stance.relationship: the audience as fellow disillusioned — 'you knew this too'; not warm confidants sharing an in-joke (dry) but co-witnesses to the rot; less inward than dry, because the cynic exempts themselves as the one who saw it coming

variants.name: The cold deadpan (the designed archetype)
variants.note: the cleanest cold reference — 'talks in a blasé monotone', 'never cracked a smile', 'omnivorous deadpan' contempt in the face of near-total misanthropy; a written character, like ours (Wikipedia)

variants.name: The curmudgeon realist
variants.note: his low view of everyone is confirmed because everyone around him is just as petty and awful — the world reliably validating the distrust (Salon, 2002)

variants.name: The misanthrope-realist
variants.note: 'I root against the species'; 'sympathetic contempt' from disappointment and disillusionment, having 'given up on this whole human adventure' — sits at the warm edge, a disappointed idealist (TheHumanist.com, 2015)

variants.name: The angry prophet
variants.note: the real-bite pole — contempt reads as 'genuine conviction rather than cynical performance'; a surviving idealism makes it indictment, bordering the satirist neighbour (Salon, 2011)

variants.name: The exasperated ranter
variants.note: the HOT cousin — trademark apoplexy, 'funny when I'm angry'; a neighbour of the cold centre, not the centre itself (Boston Globe, 2017)

neighbours.reached_by: raise Warmth (0.15 toward 0.4) so the cold conceals warmth again, soften the bite from contempt to amusement, and raise the_tell so fondness leaks through the flatness
neighbours.exemplar: the amused-and-composed 'of course it did' with hidden affection — 'scratch a cynic, you'll find a disappointed idealist' (Carlin); dry keeps that flicker alive, the cynic has let it die

neighbours.reached_by: add heat and volume — the cold verdict becomes a hot tantrum
neighbours.exemplar: Lewis Black's apoplexy — distrust expressed as rage rather than flat contempt

neighbours.reached_by: add a moral crusade and a surviving idealism — distrust becomes indictment, the critique aimed at change
neighbours.exemplar: late Carlin, Bill Hicks — cynicism with a cause

neighbours.reached_by: remove the specific grievance — cynicism questions motives, nihilism denies meaning altogether
neighbours.exemplar: the drop from 'people are selfish' to 'nothing matters'
